memo.verdict: PARK, at medium conviction. The memo recommends parking GVS-IT on the monitoring watchlist rather than progressing to Early-Stage Assessment. Four named reasons: sell-side earnings momentum grades [F] on every measured window; Element E7 (Required case simplicity guardrails) grades [D] with four of five guardrails failing; the entry point has closed, with the price at EUR 4.88 sitting 4.1% below the EUR 5.08 dashboard consensus target and 18.58% above the 200-day average; and the Risks report's own stage recommendation is hold-and-watch, which the memo adopts rather than beats. Named conditions for progression: net leverage at or below 1.8x on the Q4 2026 print excluding further debt-funded buyback; organic constant-currency revenue growth above 5.0% for two consecutive quarters; the three-month earnings revision balance turning positive; a 24-Sep-26 Business Plan carrying quantified 2026 to 2028 targets above 4.0% constant-currency growth and a dated 27% to 28% margin commitment; and a pullback toward the 200-day average near EUR 4.12. Any two firing together justifies re-running the Go-No-Go one-pager. Kill rather than park would require loss of a second original-equipment dialysis account above EUR 5m, or net leverage rising above 2.4x on further working-capital absorption.
case: The change forces are real, numerous and now evidenced in reported numbers rather than only in management commentary. Six named drivers run concurrently: Transfusion Medicine integration through full insourcing of Haemonetics whole-blood production; footprint optimisation payback from the Puerto Rico closure and the Suzhou and Lancaster ramp; Safety division expansion on respiratory protection; MedTech niche commercialisation; Life Sciences distribution; and the Mobility electric-vehicle and hydrogen pivot. Five of the six are internal and management-controlled, which raises executability.

H1 2026 supplied hard proof on three fronts. Margin: adjusted EBITDA reached 25.7%, up 62 basis points and above consensus, with Q2 at 26.8%, the highest since Q4 2021. Cash: operating cash flow more than doubled to EUR 27.5m and cash flow before working capital reached EUR 57.4m. Capital: net capital expenditure fell to EUR 16.6m from EUR 44.6m, and management formally declared the heavy build cycle complete, with normalised spend near 6% of revenue. That combination is the textbook investment-phase clearing, and the memo grades Element E8 Required Attribute RA4 Core Question 3 at [B] on it.

The corporate-change archetype is the primary setup fit at [B], with five of nine change vectors firing: balance-sheet utilisation via a EUR 19.1m five-year bullet loan at Euribor plus 1.70%; perimeter reduction via the Puerto Rico closure, the Haemotronic merger and the flattening of Safety and Energy & Mobility sub-divisions; strategy change via the explicit pivot from debt-funded acquisitions to organic execution and the 24-Sep-26 Business Plan; standards improvement via daily price-monitoring protocols, a unified Group vendor list and a 2026 to 2028 Performance Shares Plan weighting margin and net financial position at 30% each; and leadership-actor change via the commercial sales reorganisation and new MedTech sub-divisional heads. The three that do not fire are a guidance increase, a mergers-and-acquisitions step-up and a chief-executive change.
counter_case: The Risks report, produced 12-Aug-26 with completeness PASS on all 23 sections, recommends against progression. Quoted in the memo's Section F.2: "we recommend a hold-and-watch stance" rather than progressing to full capital commitment, and "GVS remains on hold-and-watch pending H2 2026 cash conversion validation and new medium-term guidance". The memo ADOPTS that recommendation and aligns its reassessment criteria to the same two gates.

The Analysis of Competing Hypotheses names FALSE FRIEND as the winning profile, with one hard inconsistency against six for the bull profile and seven for the outright-failure profile, across sixteen evidence items of which twelve are diagnostic. The aggregated 18-month to 3-year failure probability is assessed at 25% to 30%. Four false-friend mechanisms are separately evidenced: headline Transfusion Medicine growth of 10.9% masking continuing cash outflows for earn-outs and plant rationalisation; the EUR 18.7m tender offer financed by a EUR 19.1m bullet loan, improving per-share metrics while raising gross debt; adjusted EBITDA of EUR 55.4m exceeding reported EBIT by 81.6% against a peer adjustment-gap median of 15.0%, a top-5% sector divergence; and reported net profit of EUR 23.4m flattered by a EUR 6.7m unrealised currency gain while underlying operating net profit fell 9.1%. The stressed scenario gives a EUR 2.80 fair value, 35% below spot, on 22.7% margins and a 6.5x enterprise multiple.
triggers: Six key questions named for any later pass. One, does the working capital actually release? The Risks report calls this the single most diagnostic data point. Two, does MedTech organic growth turn positive from minus 0.3%, with two brokers setting 5.0% as the re-rating threshold? Three, does the Tijuana ramp deliver the promised structural gross-margin improvement, which has not been separately disclosed? Four, what does the 24-Sep-26 Business Plan commit to on quantified 2026 to 2028 growth, a dated margin target and dividend reinstatement? Five, is the earnings-quality gap closing, with adjusted EBITDA exceeding reported EBIT by 81.6% and purchase-price amortisation of EUR 6.2m due to decay? Six, how much revenue sits in unlocked commodity filtration, which no source quantifies?

Five reassessment criteria, any two firing together triggering a Go-No-Go re-run: net leverage at or below 1.8x on the Q4 2026 print excluding further debt-funded buyback; organic constant-currency growth above 5.0% for two consecutive quarters; the three-month earnings revision balance turning positive from minus 10; a 24-Sep-26 Business Plan with quantified 2026 to 2028 targets above 4.0% constant-currency growth and a dated 27% to 28% margin commitment; and a pullback toward the 200-day average near EUR 4.12, which would restore roughly 23% of upside to the consensus target.
Kill triggers: loss of a second original-equipment dialysis account above EUR 5m, or net leverage rising above 2.4x on further working-capital absorption.

Monitoring tripwires assigned: a Q3 2026 net-debt tripwire at EUR 230m and a commercial working-capital tripwire at EUR 130m, owned by the Assistant Portfolio Manager on a quarterly cadence; the Business Plan re-run owned by the Investment Analyst within five working days of 24-Sep-26. Sizing note if the case re-activates: six named drivers and a EUR 6.4m net-profit sensitivity per 5% dollar move argue for a smaller-than-standard initial position.

Carried forward for any Early-Stage Assessment carve-out: primary archetype Element E8 Required Attribute RA3, strong corporate change driven upgrade at [B]; secondary archetype Element E8 Required Attribute RA1, mis-modelled margin upgrader at [C].

Recorded data conflicts the memo surfaced rather than resolved silently: the currency drag stated as EUR 7.1m in one place and EUR 7.7m in two others, resolved arithmetically to EUR 7.7m; reported EBIT stated as both EUR 30.5m and EUR 37.5m, reconciled as reported versus adjusted; the working-capital split attributing EUR 14.2m to receivables in one report and to inventory in another; a balance-sheet working-capital expansion of EUR 20.7m against a cash absorption of EUR 21.7m, kept as two different measures; and Haemonetics consideration stated variously as USD 43.3m, USD 44.6m and EUR 42.45m, so the memo avoids the figure in any load-bearing sentence.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
